items.title: Sterlite Tech and HFCL hit 5% lower circuits again on 23 Nov, third straight fall
items.text: On 23 Nov, HFCL (Rs 177.95 on BSE) and Sterlite Technologies (Rs 591.40) were locked at the 5% lower circuit in morning trade; an HDFC Sky circuit list at 12:00 PM showed HFCL at Rs 178.60 (-5.00%) and STLTECH at Rs 590.80 (-4.99%). The headline cites falls of up to 41% from October highs. The two bellwether fibre names keep unwinding on the wider AI-stock selloff, which weighs on sentiment for the whole theme in India.

items.title: Sterlite Tech locks in 5% lower circuit at Rs 639.5 on 19 Nov on heavy delivery selling
items.text: Sterlite Technologies hit its 5% lower circuit at Rs 639.5 on 19 Nov, opening at the floor and staying there, per MarketsMojo. Delivery volume on 18 Nov was 2.94 lakh shares, up 134.63% on the 5-day average, which the article reads as genuine liquidation by holders. The stock is below its 5-, 20-, 50- and 100-day averages, while the sector rose 0.99% and the Sensex 0.42%, so the fall was stock-specific; no company news was cited as the trigger. It extends the November slide in the fibre names after the AI-stock selloff.

items.title: Vindhya Telelinks falls 3.21% to Rs 2,550.15; MarketsMojo moves valuation to 'fair' from 'attractive'
items.text: MarketsMojo says Vindhya Telelinks traded at Rs 2,550.15 on 18 Nov, down 3.21% from Rs 2,634.60. The stock is up 81.88% YTD and 58.34% over one year, with a P/E of 11.83, P/BV of 0.65 and a 52-week high of Rs 2,995.50. It cites Sterlite Technologies at a P/E of 43.78. The Mojo Grade is Hold. For investors, Vindhya is the cheaper-multiple, less re-rated name in the group, though ROCE is only 4.10%.

items.title: HFCL wins Rs 834.36 cr optical fibre cable export orders, to be executed by June 2027
items.text: HFCL secured export orders worth Rs 834.36 crore (about $88.94 million) for optical fibre cable supply through its overseas wholly owned subsidiary, from an unnamed international customer, to be executed by June 2027. The order book stood at Rs 28,900 crore at the end of the September quarter. The shares were at Rs 212.38 (+2.86%) on the page, down about 20% over the past month though up about 208% in 2026. It adds to export visibility at a time when fibre stocks have corrected sharply.

items.title: Sterlite Tech, HFCL hit lower circuits as global AI-stock rout reaches Indian fibre names
items.text: Upstox reports Sterlite Technologies hit its lower circuit at Rs 719 on 6 Nov, over 31% below its 6 Oct record but about 600% up year to date, while HFCL hit its 5% lower circuit at Rs 210, 25.3% below last month's record and up 209% YTD. Vindhya Telelinks fell 5.5% in morning trade; Birla Cable was near flat. The article ties the fall to a Thursday AI-stock sell-off (NASDAQ 100 -6.3%, Philadelphia Semiconductor index -12%) after US mid-term results raised worries about AI capex, and also to profit-booking. Most fibre stocks are 25-30% off highs, though the article notes order books remain large (Sterlite H1 FY27 order intake Rs 32,026 cr; HFCL order book Rs 28,911 cr).

items.title: Centrum, Arihant back HFCL in Diwali picks: targets Rs 290 and Rs 495
items.text: BusinessToday reports Centrum Finserve rates HFCL BUY with a target of Rs 290, and Arihant Capital Markets rates it Buy with an SOTP-based target of Rs 495. The stock traded 4.42% higher at Rs 226.90 on 4 Nov and is up 224% in 2026. The article says optical fibre cable and data-centre interconnect make up Rs 18,500 crore of the order book, nearly 70% hyperscaler-linked, and that management raised FY27 growth guidance to at least 80% YoY. Arihant's estimates put the stock at about 22.2 times FY28E EPS.

items.title: Sterlite Tech up 4.92% after Q2; CLSA Outperform Rs 1,610, Nomura Buy Rs 1,350
items.text: Sterlite Technologies closed 4.92% higher at Rs 869.80 on the BSE on 26 October, after opening at Rs 799, following its Q2 FY27 results. CLSA has an 'Outperform' with a target of Rs 1,610 (46% upside) and Nomura a 'Buy' with Rs 1,350 (25.5% upside), per Moneycontrol. Broker support after the record order book keeps the stock the sector's re-rating bellwether.

items.title: Sterlite Tech Q2 FY27 PAT Rs 517 cr, revenue Rs 2,529 cr; order book record Rs 35,274 cr
items.text: Sterlite Technologies reported Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 2,529 crore (up about 145% from Rs 1,034 crore), EBITDA of Rs 846 crore and PAT of Rs 517 crore versus Rs 4 crore a year earlier. Profit includes a one-time net gain of Rs 161 crore from a US tariff refund. The order book reached a record Rs 35,274 crore (from Rs 18,618 crore at Q1) and the company is described as net debt-free. A US jury verdict against subsidiary Sterlite Technologies Inc. is a flagged risk, under appeal. It confirms the data-centre fibre upcycle is feeding through to earnings at India's most re-rated name.

items.title: HFCL MD: data centres ~70% of fibre cable order book; order book nearly Rs 29,000 cr
items.text: In a BusinessToday interview, HFCL MD Mahendra Nahata said data centres make up about 70% of its fibre optic cable order book, with total order book almost Rs 29,000 crore, of which about Rs 19,000 crore is fibre cable. He said China Mobile and China Telecom tenders total about 150 million fibre-km, which could absorb China's manufacturing capacity, and fibre-guided drones add an estimated 70-100 million fibre-km of demand. He cited fibre prices of about $13, up from about $1.80 roughly 18 months ago, and said the preform project should improve raw-material security and margins.

sources.title: '70% is from data centres': HFCL MD Mahendra Nahata on fibre optic cable demand boom

items.title: HFCL Q2 FY27 profit up 448% to Rs 394 cr; order book above Rs 28,900 cr
items.text: HFCL reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 2,541.79 crore (+143.62% YoY) and PAT of Rs 394.22 crore (+448.14%). EBITDA was Rs 658 crore at a 25.89% margin, up 640 bps YoY. The order book exceeds Rs 28,900 crore (Q1: Rs 26,665 cr), and management guides to at least 80% FY27 revenue growth and about Rs 1,800 crore of fibre, cable and preform capex. The shares rose 5% to Rs 268.81 on 19 Oct, reinforcing the read-through that fibre demand is converting into earnings for Indian makers.

items.title: Vindhya Telelinks hits 52-week high of Rs 2,995.5 as Sensex falls 0.66%
items.text: Vindhya Telelinks rose 7.72% to an intraday high of Rs 2,995.5 on 12 Oct 2026, a 52-week high, while the Sensex fell 0.66%. MarketsMojo attributes it to technical factors and cites no company announcement. The stock is up 113.46% year to date and 116.24% over one year, so the small-cap specialty-cable name has re-rated sharply, which narrows the 'still early' argument for it.
